hints.title: Single-Use Cell Exploration
hints.text: Finding a word on a grid requires moving to adjacent cells without reusing the same cell twice in the same word. How can you explore valid character paths while temporarily marking cells as visited?

hints.title: In-Place Sentinel Invariant
hints.text: Temporarily overwrite the visited grid cell with a sentinel character like '#' during exploration, and restore its original character when returning.

hints.title: Orthogonal Backtracking Search Procedure
hints.text: Iterate through all grid cells (r, c). When board[r][c] equals word[0], start a recursive search. At step k, check boundary limits and character match. If k equals len(word) - 1, return true. Mark board[r][c] with a sentinel, explore all four orthogonal neighbors with k + 1, and restore the original character before returning false.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Branching factor is 3 after the first step because the predecessor is blocked by the sentinel.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Maintaining an auxiliary 2D visited array or set of coordinate tuples adds allocation overhead per step, whereas in-place modification uses zero extra space.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place cell mutation avoids O(M * N) memory allocations, using only O(L) call stack space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: In-place grid marking and restoration, early boundary checks before accessing grid, short-circuiting as soon as a true path is found.

solutions.approach: Four-Way Grid DFS with In-Place Restoration
